reader_question: Did younger households lose ground on owning a home?
title: The homeownership rate for householders under 35 stood at 37.0 percent in 2025, up 2.0 points from 2015 and still the lowest of five age groups.
measure_line: Homeownership rate, the share of households that own their home, by age of the householder, the person in whose name the home is owned or rented, annual averages for 2015 and 2025, the latest year and the year ten years before, United States. The scale runs from 30 to 80 percent.
notes: The rise for householders under 35 passes its margin of error, the range around the figure that sampling allows, of about 0.8 points at 90 percent confidence, and so does the rise for those 35 to 44 (2.3 points, margin 1.1). The changes for the three older groups are within their margins.
The rate for householders under 35 was highest in 2004, at 43.1 percent, and lowest in 2016, at 34.5 percent, so 2015 sits near its low.
The 2025 average leaves out October 2025, when a lapse in federal funding stopped the survey’s data collection.
alt: Slope lines show the homeownership rate of five age groups in 2015 and 2025. Householders under 35 went from 35.0 to 37.0 percent and those 35 to 44 from 58.5 to 60.8, both past their margins of error; the three older groups changed by less than their margins, from 70.0 to 69.8, 75.4 to 75.9 and 78.9 to 78.6.

table.caption: Homeownership rate by age of householder, percent

chart_notes: Householders under 35, the group the title names, are drawn in red with a dark outline; the other four groups are gray.
notes_internal: Data plan row 6 (re-picked under DR-229); window 2015 and 2025, confirmed by the data lead (A3). Data lead change 5: the 2025 average leaves out October 2025 (note 3).

Request A2 answered: census-hvs-homeownership-by-age-moe gives HVS Table B-5's margins and each change's margin (root of the summed squares, approximate). The under-35 change, 2.0, passes 0.78; 35 to 44, 2.3, passes 1.08; the three older groups do not. The title now claims the rise with its margin (DR-64, Rule 14.9), and note 1 prints the margins.
Two datasets, so the source line names both tables with each retrieval date (C2).
Note 2 gives the longer record so a reader on either side sees where 2015 sits (DR-93, DR-124).

Review fix pass: the title in ST S13's and the data lead's words; the under-35 line and its two dots take the red with the 1 px keyline on Newsprint (labels.point; data lead ruling b, D3-489, an age group no party owns); the other lines keep the context gray, since the kit has no light-fill stroke role (asked of the engineer). AX S9: householder glossed in the Census Bureau's sense and margin of error in chapter 13's words. The source line waits on the research lead's variant for the two tables (ST S11). source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey, Annual Statistics 2015 and 2025, Tables 17 and B-5, homeownership rate by age of householder with margins of error, 2015 and 2025, United States. Retrieved November 11 and 12, 2026. Survey estimates; the 2025 average leaves out October, when no data were collected; margins of the changes computed by Oath & Action.
